components.label: Pjama editor
components.summary: Standalone application for editing project maps

components.label: Pjama
components.summary: Toolkit for keeping a project map, a structured description of a project's architecture and specs, shared by developers and AI agents.

components.label: Pjama terminal manager
components.summary: All-in-one CLI/TUI app for interacting with maps, the daemon and general utilities

components.label: Pjama daemon
components.summary: Backend process that manages concurrent read and writes on maps.

components.label: Component model
components.summary: A piece of the project. Is a container for specs.

components.label: Map model
components.summary: Defines the model of the project map file in the .pjama directory at the repo root.

components.label: Layout schema
components.summary: Defines the format of the layout file in .pjama: per-user editor state such as graph node positions.

components.label: UI Elements
components.summary: UI react components made to be reusable across components in the app.

components.label: Spec model
components.summary: A quality or a property of the component that contains it.

components.label: Containment model
components.summary: Models a parent-child relationship. Signifies that the source is part of the target

components.label: Dependency model
components.summary: Models a consumer-producer relationship. Signifies that the source uses the target either entirely or part of it.

components.label: Implementation model
components.summary: Models a definition-implementation relationship. Signifies that the source takes on the specs of the target.

components.label: Map schema file
components.summary: Schema file that describes the structure of a Pjama map

components.label: Use case model
components.summary: A use case represents a sequence of actions pertinent to the component that contains it.

components.label: Interface model
components.summary: Represents a contract with an input and an output.

components.label: Type model
components.summary: Represents a type.

components.label: Item model
components.summary: Every object that lives in a map is an item.

components.label: Actor model
components.summary: Represents a use case actor

components.label: Snippet model
components.summary: Business logic given as a code snippet, in pseudocode or a real language.

components.label: Resource model
components.summary: Represents either a file or a page addressed by file path or URL.

components.label: Check model
components.summary: Checks that the actual result matches the one stated by the specs it verifies.

components.label: Decision model
components.summary: Records a choice made about the project, why it was made and why the other ones weren't.

components.label: Enforcement model
components.summary: Models a check enforcing a spec.

components.label: Derivation model
components.summary: Models a spec broken down into more granular specs.

components.label: Schema validator
components.summary: Reusable module for validating the schema

components.label: Mockup model
components.summary: A visual reference for a piece of UI, given as a resource or as inline HTML.

components.label: Technology model
components.summary: A technology, such as a language, framework or library, that the component is built with or must use.

components.label: Dev tooling
components.summary: Repo-level pnpm project that builds, typechecks, lints and tests Pjama's source.

components.label: Build
components.summary: Bundles each project with Vite.

components.label: Test runner
components.summary: Runs the colocated tests with Vitest.

components.label: Typecheck
components.summary: Typechecks source and tests with TypeScript.

components.label: Lint and format
components.summary: Lints and formats source and config files with Biome.

components.label: Claude memory
components.summary: Project memory for Claude agents, describing the pnpm scripts and when to run them.

components.label: Package manifest
components.summary: Root manifest: workspace-wide dev dependencies and the scripts the tooling exposes.

components.label: Package manager
components.summary: Installs and links the workspace packages with pnpm.

components.label: Task runner
components.summary: Runs the projects' scripts across the workspace with Nx.

components.label: Interface statement model
components.summary: A precondition, postcondition, invariant or protocol of an interface, given as text.

components.label: Step model
components.summary: One specific action of a use case.

components.label: Option model
components.summary: An alternative considered by a decision.

components.label: Parameter model
components.summary: An input or output of an interface.

components.label: Spec-to-component model
components.summary: A spec held by a component.

components.label: Step-to-use-case model
components.summary: A step of a use case.

components.label: Option-to-decision model
components.summary: An option considered by a decision.

components.label: Input-to-interface model
components.summary: An input of an interface.

components.label: Output-to-interface model
components.summary: An output of an interface.

components.label: Prerequisite-to-use-case model
components.summary: A prerequisite of a use case.

components.label: Precondition-to-interface model
components.summary: A precondition of an interface.

components.label: Postcondition-to-interface model
components.summary: A postcondition of an interface.

components.label: Invariant-to-interface model
components.summary: An invariant of an interface.

components.label: Protocol-to-interface model
components.summary: A protocol used to invoke an interface.

components.label: Criterion-to-review model
components.summary: A pass criterion of a review.

components.label: Component-to-resource model
components.summary: A resource supporting a component.

components.label: Use-case-to-actor model
components.summary: An actor taking part in a use case.

components.label: Technology-to-documentation model
components.summary: A resource documenting a technology.

components.label: Decision-to-reference model
components.summary: An item pertinent to a decision.

components.label: Decision-to-override model
components.summary: An earlier decision overridden by a decision.

components.label: Decision-to-chosen-option model
components.summary: The option chosen by a decision.

components.label: Review-to-resource model
components.summary: A resource to look at during a review.

components.label: Dependency-to-selected-spec model
components.summary: A spec passing through a dependency.

components.label: Implementation-to-excluded-spec model
components.summary: A definition spec an implementation excludes.

components.label: Step-to-next model
components.summary: The step that follows a step.

components.label: Step-to-sibling model
components.summary: The first step of an alternative branch, taken instead of a step.

components.label: Mockup-to-resource model
components.summary: The resource a mockup shows.

components.label: Interface relationship models
components.summary: Relationships linking an interface to its parameters and statements.

components.label: Use case relationship models
components.summary: Relationships linking a use case to its steps, prerequisites and actors, and steps to each other.

components.label: Decision relationship models
components.summary: Relationships linking a decision to its options, chosen option, references and overrides.

components.label: Review relationship models
components.summary: Relationships linking a review to its criteria and resources.

components.label: Resource relationship models
components.summary: Relationships linking components, technologies and mockups to resources.

components.label: Spec membership relationship models
components.summary: Relationships placing a spec in a component, or in a dependency's or implementation's selection.

components.label: Secondary item models
components.summary: Items that exist only in function of another item: interface statements and parameters, use case prerequisites and steps, decision options and review criteria.

components.label: Use case prerequisite model
components.summary: A condition assumed to hold for a use case to apply, given as text.

components.label: Review criterion model
components.summary: A pass criterion of a review, given as text.

relations.label: Daemon reads and writes the map file
Untitled relation
relations.summary: Implementation of the map schema as JSON Schema

relations.label: Test script runs the typecheck first
Test script runs the lint first
Build script runs the typecheck first
Build script runs the lint first

actors.label: Developer
actors.summary: Person responsible for the project who shapes its map: structure, specs and decisions.

actors.label: AI agent
actors.summary: Coding agent working in the repo that reads the map for context and keeps it in sync with the code.

actors.label: CI pipeline
actors.summary: Automated pipeline that checks the map stays valid and consistent with the repo.

requirements.label: Map lives in the repo
requirements.summary: The map is a plain file versioned with the code and readable without Pjama installed.

requirements.label: No silent lost edits
requirements.summary: Simultaneous changes from developers and agents can overwrite each other but never silently.

requirements.label: Always valid
requirements.summary: Every write made through Pjama leaves the map schema-valid with all references resolved.

requirements.label: Changes reach every client
requirements.summary: Each open client sees changes made elsewhere within a few seconds, without a manual reload.

requirements.label: Agent parity
requirements.summary: Every operation a developer can perform is also available to agents through a non-interactive command.

requirements.label: Local and offline
requirements.summary: All Pjama tools run on the developer's machine, with no network access or account required.

requirements.label: Incoming changes are visible
requirements.summary: Developers and agents have visibility over the changes others make to the map.

requirements.label: Changes can be reviewed and reverted
requirements.summary: Developers can review changes, in detail or in bulk, and revert the ones they reject.

requirements.label: Atomic operations
requirements.summary: Applies each change as one item- or field-level operation, rejecting any that would leave the map invalid.

requirements.label: Broadcasts changes
requirements.summary: Pushes every applied operation to all connected clients as it happens.

requirements.label: Operation log
requirements.summary: Keeps a persistent log of every operation: author, time, item, field, and before and after values.

requirements.label: Reverts operations
requirements.summary: Reverts any logged operation by applying its inverse as a new operation.

requirements.label: Changes since a point
requirements.summary: Returns every operation after a given position in the log, so each client can track what it has already seen.

requirements.label: Detects external edits
requirements.summary: Watches the map file and logs changes made outside Pjama as item- and value-level operations authored as external.

requirements.label: No save step
requirements.summary: Each edit is sent as soon as it is finished; there is no batching or save button.

requirements.label: Protects the field being edited
requirements.summary: A remote change to the field being edited waits until editing ends, then is offered as keep mine or take theirs.

requirements.label: Shows incoming changes
requirements.summary: Items and fields get highlighted when they change and marked as "Unseen" (similar to what happens with "Unread" emails).

requirements.label: Mapping depth threshold
requirements.summary: The map covers the project at the granularity the developer chooses; unmapped code and tests are normal, not gaps. Exceptions are at dev or agent discretion.

requirements.label: Layout stays local
requirements.summary: The layout file is never committed: it holds one user's editor state, not project information.

requirements.label: Displays changes to review
requirements.summary: When a change that needs to be reviewed comes to the editor, the user can either accept or reject it, one by one and in bulk.

requirements.label: Auto-review
requirements.summary: Users can set that incoming changes pending for a review get automatically approved.

requirements.label: Editing capabilities
requirements.summary: The editor allows the developer to create, delete and move all item types, allows to edit each field and reference present in any item.

requirements.label: Item pages
requirements.summary: Each item has it's own page from where it's possible to edit all it's fields and references.

requirements.label: Lists all items
requirements.summary: The page shows all items in a sidebar.

requirements.label: One item at a time
requirements.summary: Only a single item's page is displayed at a time.

requirements.label: Item are links
requirements.summary: All item names, references and ids that appear on screen are clickable links to that item page.

requirements.label: Sidebar folders
requirements.summary: The developer can organize items in the sidebar trough folders.

requirements.label: Divided item sections
requirements.summary: Items in the sidebar are divided by type.

requirements.label: Moving specs
requirements.summary: Specs can be moved between components by drag-and-drop.

requirements.label: Elements must be reusable
requirements.summary: Elements are made to be reusable across the entire editor and potentially other Pjama UIs.

requirements.label: Consistent UX
requirements.summary: Elements serve to enforce a consistent UX across the UI and between other elements themselves.

requirements.label: Text input
requirements.summary: The field allows for direct text input.

requirements.label: Cursor position on edit
requirements.summary: On edit the cursor is placed at the end of the "text" in the field

requirements.label: The field stores multiple values
requirements.summary: The field must support storing multiple text values

requirements.label: Value as pill
requirements.summary: Values stored in the field are displayed as pills

requirements.label: Autocomplete
requirements.summary: While typing, the field proposes autocomplete options based on the other values that the field assumes across the map. Closer matches are proposed first.

requirements.label: Value pills removal
requirements.summary: While in edit mode, value pills can be removed by a single click, by pressing backspace with the cursor after it or by pressing del with the cursor before it.

requirements.label: Directed edge
requirements.summary: A relationship is a directed edge between a source node and a target node.

requirements.label: All specs pass
requirements.summary: All the specs of the source can be seen by the target and vice versa

requirements.label: Source is child
requirements.summary: The source node is also called "Child".

requirements.label: Target is parent
requirements.summary: The target node is also called "Parent".

requirements.label: Only selected specs pass
requirements.summary: The selected specs of the source can be seen by the target and the selected specs of the target can be seen by the source.

requirements.label: Source is consumer
requirements.summary: The source node is also called "Consumer".

requirements.label: Target is producer
requirements.summary: The target node is also called "Producer".

requirements.label: Spec selection
requirements.summary: The relationship must be able to select none. some or all specs from either node independently.

requirements.label: Target specs pass
requirements.summary: All the specs of the target can be seen by the source, except the excluded ones, but not vice versa.

requirements.label: Allow no selection
requirements.summary: Even if it doesn't make sense, the model must allow a dependency to not select any spec. This should be flagged in the lint skill as a smell.

requirements.label: Source is Implementation
requirements.summary: The source node is also called "Implementation".

requirements.label: Target is Definition
requirements.summary: The target node is also called "Definition".

requirements.label: Derived specs
requirements.summary: A spec can be derived from one or more specs.

requirements.label: Allow underived
requirements.summary: The schema must allow underived specs.

requirements.label: Flag underived
requirements.summary: A semantic analysis of the map should flag an underived spec if it judges it's not foundational.

requirements.label: Top-level specs
requirements.summary: An underived spec is generally considered as foundational to the system.

requirements.label: Single component
requirements.summary: Each spec must be assigned to one and only one component.

requirements.label: Checkability
requirements.summary: Each spec should be associated to one or more checks that ensure the spec is respected by the code.

requirements.label: Allow unchecked
requirements.summary: The schema must allow unchecked specs.

requirements.label: Flag unchecked
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map should flag unchecked specs.

requirements.label: A requirement should be atomic
requirements.summary: Requirements should make atomic statements. If a statement can be decomposed, each piece should become it's own requirement.

requirements.label: Flag non-atomic requirements
requirements.summary: A semantic analysis of the map should flag requirements that it thinks could be decomposed.

requirements.label: Branches in the sequence
requirements.summary: Each step of the sequence may branch into alternative sequences.

requirements.label: Merge the branches
requirements.summary: Each branch may be merged into another sequence, usually the originating one.

requirements.label: Early termination
requirements.summary: Each branch may terminate early compared to the other ones.

requirements.label: Actors
requirements.summary: Each use case may have one or more actors.

requirements.label: Allow no actors
requirements.summary: A schema must allow a use case to have no actors.

requirements.label: Flag no actors
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map should flag use cases without actors.

requirements.label: Prerequisites
requirements.summary: A use case may have one, or more prerequisites that indicate conditions or properties that are assumed to be valid for the use case to apply.

requirements.label: Type kinds
requirements.summary: A type can be a primitive, a struct, an array, a union (one of several types), a merge (all the properties of several structs) or a constant.

requirements.label: Custom definition
requirements.summary: The user can define custom types.

requirements.label: Input and output
requirements.summary: Interfaces should have inputs and an outputs.

requirements.label: Use types
requirements.summary: Interfaces describe inputs and outputs through types.

requirements.label: Recursive types
requirements.summary: A type can be defined recursively.

requirements.label: Preconditions, postconditions and invariants
requirements.summary: An interface may state it's own pre- and postconditions and invariants.

requirements.label: Protocols
requirements.summary: An interface may state the protocols that are used to invoke it.

requirements.label: Multiple uses
requirements.summary: The same actor may be used in multiple use cases of the same schema.

requirements.label: Language
requirements.summary: Snippets may be associated to a known language.

requirements.label: Code body
requirements.summary: Snippets are given in a free form text-based body.

requirements.label: Allow missing inputs/outputs
requirements.summary: The schema allows interfaces with missing inputs/outputs.

requirements.label: Flag missing inputs/outputs
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map should flag interfaces with no inputs/outputs.

requirements.label: Contains specs
requirements.summary: A component may contain any number of specs.

requirements.label: Allow no specs
requirements.summary: The schema allows components to have no specs.

requirements.label: Flag no specs
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map flags components without specs.

requirements.label: Path or URL
requirements.summary: A resource can be addressed either via file path or URL.

requirements.label: Path format
requirements.summary: Paths are given relative to the root of the project, in POSIX format.

requirements.label: Project root
requirements.summary: The root of the project is defined in the map relatively to the position of the map.

requirements.label: Includes resources
requirements.summary: A component may include any amount of resources.

requirements.label: Action
requirements.summary: A dependency may state the action it represents. The default is "uses".

requirements.label: No self-relationships
requirements.summary: Source and target are different items.

requirements.label: Allow containment cycles
requirements.summary: The schema allows containment relationships to form a cycle, where a component ends up, directly or indirectly, part of itself.

requirements.label: Flag containment cycles
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map flags containment cycles.

requirements.label: Allow implementation cycles
requirements.summary: The schema allows implementation relationships to form a cycle, where a component ends up, directly or indirectly, implementing itself.

requirements.label: Flag implementation cycles
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map flags implementation cycles.

requirements.label: Enforces specs
requirements.summary: A check enforces that one or more specs are respected in code.

requirements.label: No unlinked checks
requirements.summary: A map must not contain checks not associated to any spec.

requirements.label: Results
requirements.summary: Running a check produces a pass or fail result and a date+time.

requirements.label: Rationale
requirements.summary: A decision states the reason that one option was chosen over the others.

requirements.label: Options
requirements.summary: A decision may list possible alternative options.

requirements.label: References
requirements.summary: A decision may reference the items pertinent to it.

requirements.label: Allow no references
requirements.summary: The schema allows decisions that reference no item.

requirements.label: Flag no references
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map may flag decisions that don't reference any item.

requirements.label: Override
requirements.summary: A decision may override a previous conflicting one, and both stay in the map.

requirements.label: Identified by UUID
requirements.summary: Items are identified by a random UUID.

requirements.label: Derived status
requirements.summary: A decision's status is derived: overridden if another decision overrides it, otherwise closed if it is marked closed or has a chosen option, otherwise open.

requirements.label: Containment is transitive
requirements.summary: If A is part of B and B is part of C then A is also part of C.

requirements.label: Many-to-one
requirements.summary: Source to target relate N:1 (A child can have only one parent.

requirements.label: Many-to-many
requirements.summary: Source to target relate N:N.

requirements.label: Many-to-many
requirements.summary: Source to target relate N:N.

requirements.label: Item to item
requirements.summary: Source and target are two items.

requirements.label: Component nodes
requirements.summary: Source and target are two components.

requirements.label: Component nodes
requirements.summary: Source and target are two components.

requirements.label: Component nodes
requirements.summary: Source and target are two components.

requirements.label: Check-to-spec
requirements.summary: Source is a check. Target is a spec.

requirements.label: Many-to-many
requirements.summary: Source to target relate N:N.

requirements.label: Flag many-to-one
requirements.summary: A semantic analysis of the map should flag a check if it determines it covers separated aspects from different specs.

requirements.label: Use-case-to-actor
requirements.summary: Source is a use case, target is an actor.

requirements.label: Many-to-many
requirements.summary: Source to target relate N:N.

requirements.label: Custom != constant
requirements.summary: Custom types are different from constants and the two should be clearly differentiated when displayed.

requirements.label: Spec-to-spec
requirements.summary: Both source and target are specs.

requirements.label: Many-to-many
requirements.summary: Source to target relate N:N.

requirements.label: Source is derived
requirements.summary: The source node is also called "Derived".

requirements.label: Target is origin
requirements.summary: The target node is also called "Origin".

requirements.label: Relationship types
requirements.summary: There are different types of relationships.

requirements.label: Item types
requirements.summary: There are different types of items.

requirements.label: Spec types
requirements.summary: There are different types of specs.

requirements.label: Spec categories
requirements.summary: Specs may be assigned to a category, a free-form string. A map's categories are the set of those used across its specs.

requirements.label: Validation failure cascade
requirements.summary: A spec that fails validation impact all specs it's derived from.

requirements.label: Sequence of steps
requirements.summary: A use case is structured as a sequence of steps, linked through next and sibling relationships.

requirements.label: Extensible
requirements.summary: Tests can be defined by the user through plugins.

requirements.label: Modular validation
requirements.summary: A static analysis of the map must take into account schemas provided by the loaded plugins, if present.

requirements.label: Check states
requirements.summary: Checks can be in 3 states: "Not checked", "Passing" and "Failing".

requirements.label: Not checked until execution
requirements.summary: A test is marked as "Not checked" until it's related code is run. At which point will be either "Passing" or "Failing".

requirements.label: Manual check
requirements.summary: Reviews are meant to be manual checks that must be assesed by a human or an agent. Because of this reviews are not easily repeatable.

requirements.label: Automated checks
requirements.summary: Tests are meant to be linked to code and scripts and thus represent a check that is automated and easily repeatable.

requirements.label: Reviewers
requirements.summary: "Passing" and "failing" reviews are associated to the user or agent that performed them.

requirements.label: Test and plugins
requirements.summary: Tests are associated to their plugin to match them easily to their automated validation.

requirements.label: Map model structure
requirements.summary: Uses the specifications given in the map model to define it's structure.

requirements.label: Basic type validation
requirements.summary: The schema performs only basic type validation: no cardinality, reference or cross-item checks.

requirements.label: Items and relationships
requirements.summary: Items and relationships live in two top-level lists.

requirements.label: Strict structural validation
requirements.summary: The tool enforces the base structure of the schema plus the numerosity constraints of relationships

requirements.label: Not a static analysis
requirements.summary: The validator doesn't operate as a linter/statical analyzer. All the flagged checks described in the model are out of scope.

requirements.label: Pass/fail output
requirements.summary: The output of the validator is strictly pass-or-fail

requirements.label: Error messages
requirements.summary: Failing outputs are implemented as errors carrying specific information on the reason the validation failed.

requirements.label: Spec exclusion
requirements.summary: An implementation may exclude any of the definition's specs. Excluded specs don't pass to the source.

requirements.label: No check results
requirements.summary: Check results, states and reviewers are not stored in the map.

requirements.label: Optional notes
requirements.summary: Relationships may have free form notes.

requirements.label: Map identity
requirements.summary: A map has a UUID, a name and a slug.

requirements.label: Map slug
requirements.summary: The slug is derived from the map name: diacritics dropped, other symbols removed, spaces collapsed, letters lowercased and spaces turned into hyphens.
requirements.notes: The slug is derived from the map name by dropping diacritics (keeping the base letter), removing all other symbols except letters, digits and spaces, collapsing repeated spaces, lowercasing all letters and turning the remaining spaces into hyphens.

requirements.label: User-defined primitives
requirements.summary: Primitive names are free-form, so the map isn't tied to one language's type system.

requirements.label: Literal constants
requirements.summary: Constants are written as literals.

requirements.label: Unique ids
requirements.summary: Item ids should never collide.

requirements.label: Portable across systems
requirements.summary: A map works the same on every operating system the repository is checked out on.

requirements.label: Steps form a rooted DAG
requirements.summary: The steps of a use case form a directed acyclic graph with a single root, where the sequence starts.

requirements.label: Close without choosing
requirements.summary: A decision may be marked closed without choosing an option, when none of its options is correct.

requirements.label: Schema version
requirements.summary: A map states the schema version it is written in, as v<MAJ>.<MIN>.<PATCH>.

requirements.label: Field descriptions
requirements.summary: The schema carries JSON Schema descriptions that convey what a field means beyond its type, e.g. that an input's name is the parameter's name.

requirements.label: Parameter names
requirements.summary: Interface inputs are always named. Outputs may be unnamed.

requirements.label: Criteria
requirements.summary: A review states its pass criteria as a list of statements.

requirements.label: Resources
requirements.summary: A review may list the resources to look at.

requirements.label: Required reviewer
requirements.summary: A review may require to be performed by a human or by an agent.

requirements.label: Free-form instructions
requirements.summary: A review may give instructions on how to carry it out as free-form text, rendered as markdown.

requirements.label: Markdown notes
requirements.summary: Relationship notes are free-form text, rendered as markdown.

requirements.label: Visual reference
requirements.summary: A mockup shows how a piece of UI should look, from a rough wireframe to a high-fidelity design.

requirements.label: Resource or inline HTML
requirements.summary: A mockup shows either a resource, through a mockup-to-resource relationship, or inline HTML.

requirements.label: Resource content
requirements.summary: A resource mockup shows the resource as an image or as an HTML document, depending on its format.

requirements.label: Inline HTML
requirements.summary: An HTML mockup is given as an inline body, either a fragment of elements or a full HTML document.

requirements.label: Wrapped fragments
requirements.summary: An HTML fragment is rendered inside a blank HTML document.

requirements.label: Isolated rendering
requirements.summary: HTML mockups are rendered isolated from the app displaying them, so their markup and styles can't affect it.

requirements.label: No scripts
requirements.summary: Scripts in HTML mockups, inline or from a file, are never executed.

requirements.label: Project files only
requirements.summary: A resource path points to a file inside the project.

requirements.label: Type visibility
requirements.summary: A spec may only reference types visible to its component: the ones it owns and the ones reaching it through flows.

requirements.label: Scoped names
requirements.summary: Type names are unique only within their component. Two components may each define a type with the same name.

requirements.label: Visible types
requirements.summary: An interface's inputs and outputs only use types visible to its component.

requirements.label: Constraints
requirements.summary: A spec states a constraint on the component that holds it.

requirements.label: Supporting material
requirements.summary: Resources are standalone supporting material. They don't take part in spec flows.

requirements.label: Named technology
requirements.summary: A technology spec states the name of the technology it's about, separately from the spec's own name.

requirements.label: Version
requirements.summary: A technology spec may state the version or version range of the technology, in free form.

requirements.label: Documentation
requirements.summary: A technology spec may reference resources documenting the technology.

requirements.label: Closed structures
requirements.summary: The schema rejects fields it doesn't define, except in plugin-specific settings.

requirements.label: Case-insensitive UUIDs
requirements.summary: The schema accepts UUIDs written in either uppercase or lowercase hex.

requirements.label: Sources in src
requirements.summary: Source code lives in `src/`.

requirements.label: Single-file apps

decisions.label: Partial mapping by design
decisions.summary: The map is not meant to mirror every piece of code or every test; the developer decides how deep it goes.
decisions.notes: Some tests sit at a granularity the developer does not want to map; others cover behavior at the right level that no spec expresses yet. Forcing full coverage would bloat the map or invent specs. Consequences: verification checks that mapped items are true, never flags unmapped ones as drift; agents link tests only where a spec matches, and propose a spec otherwise.

decisions.label: Plain random UUIDs as item ids
decisions.summary: Items are identified by plain random UUIDs with no type prefix. An item's type lives only in its `type` field.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed.

**Chosen: plain random UUIDs (v4).** They can't overflow, keep the standard `uuid` format and don't duplicate the `type` field. The CLIs, scripts and MCPs that will work on the map resolve ids by themselves, and the field holding a reference almost always implies the type it points to.

**Rejected options:**
- **Progressive prefixed ids** (e.g. `REQ-001`, the projMap format). A fixed-width counter eventually overflows, and progressive ids collide when a map is edited concurrently or merged.
- **Type-prefixed UUIDs** (e.g. `req_<uuid>`). It duplicates the `type` field, which it can then disagree with, and it drops the standard `uuid` format. The schema check it enables only covers the shape of a reference, not its existence, and reference checks are out of the schema's scope anyway (REQ-162).

decisions.label: Decision options identified by UUIDs
decisions.summary: Each option of a decision carries its own UUID, and the chosen option is referenced by it.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed.

**Chosen: a UUID per option.** The reference to the chosen option survives reordering, renaming and deleting the other options.

**Rejected options:**
- **Index into the options list.** Reordering or deleting an option silently makes the decision point to a different choice, and nothing in the index tells tooling what it originally meant.
- **Option name.** Renaming an option breaks the reference, and names aren't guaranteed to be unique within a decision.

decisions.label: How reviews point at what to look at
decisions.summary: Whether a review derives what to look at from the graph, lists it explicitly, or both.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** open. To be decided through use.

**Context:** a review's subject can be derived from the graph (review → enforced specs → host components → their resources). But a resource is not always in the right component: resources are accessories to the system, with far fewer guardrails against misuse than components and specs.

**Interim:** the review lists the resources to look at, with nothing derived from the graph (REQ-188).

**Options:**
- **Derived only.** Nothing to keep in sync, and granularity follows the map (D-001): a review that needs a single file calls for a finer component. Relies on resources being attached to the right components.
- **Explicit only.** The review lists what to look at. Precise, but the list goes stale silently when the map changes, and it is a second, unmapped way to say where things are.
- **Derived plus additional resources.** The derived subject covers the common case, the explicit list covers resources that don't sit in the right component. Risks becoming the default way to point reviews at files, bypassing the map.

decisions.label: Resources are project files or URLs
decisions.summary: A resource either points to a file inside the project, by path, or to a web page, by URL. The map stores no files of its own.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed.

**Chosen: project files and URLs only.** Pjama is local-first: the map lives in the repository with the files it points to, so every resource it references by path is there on every machine the repository is checked out on.

**Rejected options:**
- **Attachments stored with the map** (files dragged into a resource and kept in an assets folder next to the map), alongside links. It would make maps easier to move, but having two modes means two sets of consequences: whether the file follows its original, what happens when it's moved, what deleting the resource deletes. Prototyping the creation flow showed those consequences are confusing, and making them clear clutters the UI.
- **Any path on the filesystem.** Paths outside the project don't exist on other machines, which breaks the map for everyone else.

**Consequence: importing files from outside the project.** When a user brings in a file from outside the project, the UI asks where in the project to put a copy, offering `.pjama/assets/` as the default when the user doesn't want to choose. The copy is then a normal project file, and the resource links to it by path.

decisions.label: Types are specs
decisions.summary: Types are specs with a single owner component and are shared through flows, instead of living in a map-wide list.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed.

**Chosen: types as single-owner specs.** A type belongs to the component that defines it and reaches other components through flows like any other spec. Types stay compartmentalized: a component's local types (e.g. React props) don't flood a global namespace, and encapsulation keeps them private.

**Where shared types live:**
- A concept with a clear authority (e.g. `Order`) lives in the component owning the concept, and others import it or see it through emergence.
- System-wide vocabulary (e.g. `Uuid`, `Money`) lives in the system's root component and reaches everything through refinement.
- A contract between peers (e.g. a wire format) lives in a component for that contract, imported by each side.
- Two components needing the same type either depend on one another (one owns, the other imports; a missing edge is a gap in the map) or share a contract component. When they are meant to diverge, one copies the type as a one-off action: the copy is independent and not linked to the original. Tracing a copy's origin is an open point (see `docs/implementation.md`).

**Rejected options:**
- **A map-wide list of types.** No ownership, and every local type ends up in one global namespace.
- **Multiple owners for shared types.** A spec would have more than one origin, so deactivations, opt-outs and failure cascades would have no single place to apply.
- **A catch-all component for shared types** (like a `types.ts`). It is named after what it holds rather than what it describes, and becomes a drawer. A contract component is different: it is a real part of the system that can change, break and be checked.
- **Referencing a type across components with no edge between them.** It hides a coupling the map should show.
- **Copy plus a derivation back to the original.** Derivation means breaking a spec down into more granular ones, and its failure cascade (REQ-148) would wrongly reach the original.

decisions.label: Flat map
decisions.summary: A map is two flat collections, items and relationships. Every reference outside an atomic value is a relationship.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed.

**Chosen: items and relationships only.** Specs, steps, options, parameters and statements are items; whatever linked them (nesting, id lists, id fields) is a relationship. Every edit is then a create, delete, set or unset on one entity, deleting an item deletes the relationships touching it, and the file, the edit model and an in-memory store share one shape.

**Rejected options:**
- **Nested lists** (specs inside components, steps inside use cases). Each nesting level needs its own list operations, and diffing an external edit means first working out where nested things went.
- **Id arrays as fields** (e.g. `selectedSpecs`). Deleting an item means finding and editing every array that mentions it, and references come in two forms.
- **One collection per item kind.** Splitting by kind, or by importance, is a presentation concern whose boundary moves; promoting a type would be a migration.

decisions.label: Identity and optional fields
decisions.summary: Fields are either identity fields, required with no default, or optional. Nothing has a default value.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed.

**Chosen: two tiers.** Identity fields (id, type, source, target) carry entity-defining information and can't be preset. Everything else is optional: absent means unset, and the UI shows a placeholder (e.g. "Untitled component"). Creating an entity needs only its identity fields, and empty and absent stop being two ways of saying the same thing.

**Rejected options:**
- **Required fields with defaults.** Every type would need defaults defined, and readers must handle missing optional fields anyway.

decisions.label: Ordered relationship types
decisions.summary: Orderability is a property of a relationship type. Ordered relationships carry an optional fractional position, never rebalanced.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed.

**Chosen: variable-length fractional keys on the relationship.** Inserting or reordering is one set on one relationship; concurrent inserts at the same spot both succeed. Keys grow only when a gap is exhausted, and lists are user-ordered and short, so no rebalancing is ever needed and no edit happens outside the normal channels. The position sits on the relationship, next to the reference to what it orders within, so moving a spec to another component is a single relationship edit.

**Rejected options:**
- **Ordered list fields.** Elements need value identity, duplicates must be forbidden and inserts anchor to neighbours.
- **Fixed-width keys with rebalancing.** Rebalancing rewrites every sibling's key, an edit no user made.
- **Orderability per relationship.** Two relationships of the same type could disagree.

decisions.label: No type registry yet
decisions.summary: Item and relationship types are defined by the map model and versioned with the schema. A registry waits for extensibility.
decisions.notes:
**Status:** closed, until extensibility work starts.

**Chosen: types live in the map model.** Type definitions, orderability, allowed endpoints and dependent types are written in the map model's specs and checked by validation scripts.

**Deferred:** a type registry, per-type versions with accepted version ranges, inline user-defined types, keeping entities of unknown types untouched, and migrating types between versions.
